quandoUsar: Standalone sign-in card on your own page, with email plus a 6-digit code as the main path and passkey and three single sign-on providers as alternatives.
Prototypes that need a navigable sign-in flow without a backend: submit, verification, and providers are simulated with timers.
When it is worth fixing common domain mistakes in the email: “gmial.com” becomes the suggestion “gmail.com”, applied with one click.
quandoEvitar: Use `login-centered` when the login takes the full screen, passkey should come first, or the same card needs to switch to account creation.
Use `signup-form` to create an account with name, password, and terms acceptance.
Use `otp-input` when you already have the flow and only need the code field.

teclado.acao: In the email field, moves on to the code; in a code cell, submits the verification, which also fires on its own when all 6 cells are filled.
On the code step, move focus between the cells (`otp-input` behavior).
In an empty code cell, clears the previous one and moves focus back to it.
Moves through the controls of the step; the resend button stays focusable during the countdown, with `aria-disabled`.

acessibilidade: Each step change is announced by a hidden `role="status"` region with `aria-live="polite"`; the visible status line in the footer is `aria-hidden`.
Focus follows the flow: first code cell, welcome heading on completion, and the email field, with its text selected, when changing email or leaving.
The providers form a named `role="group"` with an `aria-label` per button, the resend says in its `aria-label` how many seconds remain, and the domain suggestion is a “Use …” button.
movimento: Steps cross sideways coming out of a slight blur, returning from the opposite side, and the card height follows the new step on a spring that does not overshoot only during the switch.
On completion via the code, the small avatar grows into the large one (shared layout), a ring draws around it, a checkmark badge appears, and the title, details, and button rise in sequence.
With “reduce motion” on, steps only fade, the height changes instantly, and the avatar, ring, and badge appear without animation.
responsivo: The card uses `min(100%, 432px)`; a container query up to 380 px tightens margins, title, and provider buttons, and up to 480 px of viewport the radius shrinks.
desempenho: A `ResizeObserver` measures the content to animate the height and the resend countdown uses a 1 s timer only on the code step; timers are cleared on unmount.
notasIA: Nothing is actually authenticated: `submitEmail`, `verify`, and `signInWith` use `setTimeout` and `onSignIn(account, method)` only signals the end of the simulation; replace these functions with the real calls.
There are only two props, `demoCode` (default `123456`, shown as a hint in the code field) and `onSignIn`; remove the hint in production and note that the texts are hardcoded in English.
Depends on `avatar`, `button`, `input`, and `otp-input`; the footer's “Sign up” only changes the status line, so hook it up to your signup route, for example with `signup-form`.
